sentences.l: And the slave feared for himself the perishing, so he struck Queen Abrīza with his sword and killed her from the violence of his rage, and mounted his steed and headed to the state of his way.
sentences.i: The slave feared for his life. He struck Queen Abrīza with his sword and killed her in the violence of his rage, then mounted his horse and went his way.
sentences.n: khashiya ʿalā nafsihi, “to fear for oneself”. tawajjaha ilā ḥāli sabīlihi, “he went off about his business”, a stock phrase for leaving the scene.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ مَارَاحَ الْعَبْدُ انْكَشَفَ الْغُبَارُ عَنْ جَدِّكَ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ فَرَأَى أُمَّكَ ابْنَتَهُ وَهِيَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ قَتِيلَةٌ وَعَلَى الْأَرْضِ جَدِيلَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda mā rāḥa al-ʿabdu inkashafa al-ghubāru ʿan jaddika al-maliki Ḥardūba maliki al-Rūmi fa-raʾā ummaka ibnatahu wa-hiya fī dhālika al-makāni qatīlatun wa-ʿalā al-arḍi jadīlatun
sentences.l: And after the slave went, the dust uncovered-itself from your grandfather King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm; and he saw your mother, his daughter, and she in that place slain, and on the ground thrown-down.
sentences.i: After the slave had gone, the dust parted to reveal your grandfather, King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm. He saw your mother, his daughter, lying slain in that place, cast down on the ground.
sentences.n: The print runs mā rāḥa together (ماراح); baʿda mā, “after”. rāḥa, “to go off”, is colloquial in flavour. inkashafa al-ghubāru ʿan, “the dust cleared away from”, the stock phrase for revealing who is coming. jadīla, “thrown to the ground”, from jadala, chosen to rhyme with qatīla, “slain”.

sentences.t: فَصَعُبَ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ وَكَبُرَ لَدَيْهِ وَسَأَلَنِي عَنْ سَبَبِ قَتْلِهَا وَعَنْ سَبَبِ خُرُوجِهَا خُفْيَةً مِنْ بِلَادِ أَبِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣaʿuba dhālika ʿalayhi wa-kabura ladayhi wa-saʾalanī ʿan sababi qatlihā wa-ʿan sababi khurūjihā khufyatan min bilādi abīhā
sentences.l: And that was-hard upon him and was-great with him, and he asked me about the cause of her killing and about the cause of her going-out secretly from the lands of her father.
sentences.i: It went hard with him and weighed heavily on him, and he asked me why she had been killed and why she had slipped away in secret from her father's land.
sentences.n: ṣaʿuba ʿalayhi wa-kabura ladayhi, “it was hard for him and great in his eyes”, a rhyming pair (ʿalayhi / ladayhi) for grief.

sentences.t: فَحَكَيْتُ لَهُ جَمِيعَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ وَهَذَا هُوَ سَبَبُ الْعَدَاوَةِ بَيْنَ أَهْلِ بِلَادِ الرُّومِ وَبَيْنَ أَهْلِ بِلَادِ بَغْدَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakaytu lahu jamīʿa dhālika mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri wa-hādhā huwa sababu al-ʿadāwati bayna ahli bilādi al-Rūmi wa-bayna ahli bilādi Baghdāda
sentences.l: So I told him all of that from the first to the last; and this is the cause of the enmity between the people of the lands of the Rūm and the people of the lands of Baghdad.
sentences.i: I told him the whole story from beginning to end, and that is the cause of the enmity between the people of the land of the Rūm and the people of the land of Baghdad.
sentences.n: bayna … wa-bayna, “between … and”, repeating bayna before the second term, is common in this text.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ احْتَمَلْنَا أُمَّكَ وَهِيَ قَتِيلَةٌ وَدَفَنَّاهَا وَقَدِ احْتَمَلْتُكَ أَنَا وَرَبَّيْتُكَ وَعَلَّقْتُ لَكَ الْخَرَزَةَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ مَعَ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika iḥtamalnā ummaka wa-hiya qatīlatun wa-dafannāhā wa-qad iḥtamaltuka anā wa-rabbaytuka wa-ʿallaqtu laka al-kharazata allatī kānat maʿa al-malikati Abrīzata
sentences.l: And at that we carried your mother, she being slain, and buried her; and I carried you, I, and raised you, and hung for you the bead that had been with Queen Abrīza.
sentences.i: Then we took up your mother's body and buried her. I carried you away myself and brought you up, and I hung on you the bead that Queen Abrīza had kept.
sentences.n: ʿallaqtu laka, “I hung for you”, that is, round your neck as an amulet.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا كَبِرْتَ وَبَلَغْتَ مَبْلَغَ الرِّجَالِ لَمْ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُخْبِرَكَ بِحَقِيقَةِ الْأَمْرِ لِأَنَّنِي لَوْ أَخْبَرْتُكَ بِذَلِكَ لَثَارَتْ بَيْنَكُمُ الْحُرُوبُ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā kabirta wa-balaghta mablagha al-rijāli lam yumkinunī an ukhbiraka bi-ḥaqīqati al-amri li-annanī law akhbartuka bi-dhālika la-thārat baynakumu al-ḥurūbu
sentences.l: And when you grew-big and reached the reaching-point of men, it was not possible-for-me to tell you the truth of the matter, because if I had told you that, the wars would have flared up between you.
sentences.i: When you grew up and came to manhood, I could not tell you how things truly stood, for had I told you, war would have broken out between you.
sentences.n: lam yumkinunī: after lam Classical requires the jussive, lam yumkinnī; the print's two separate nūns keep the indicative ending -u, a Middle Arabic habit. baynakum, “between you (plural)”, means between you and your father's house in Baghdad.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَمَرَنِي جَدُّكَ بِالْكِتْمَانِ وَلَا قُدْرَةَ لِي عَلَى مُخَالَفَةِ أَمْرِ جَدِّكَ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad amaranī jadduka bi-al-kitmāni wa-lā qudrata lī ʿalā mukhālafati amri jaddika al-maliki Ḥardūba maliki al-Rūmi
sentences.l: And your grandfather ordered me to the concealment, and there is no power to me over going-against the command of your grandfather King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm.
sentences.i: Your grandfather ordered me to keep it hidden, and I had no power to go against the command of your grandfather, King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm.
sentences.n: lā qudrata lī ʿalā, “I have no power to”.

sentences.t: فَهَذَا سَبَبُ كِتْمَانِ الْخَبَرِ عَنْكَ وَعَدَمِ إِعْلَامِكَ بِأَنَّ أَبَاكَ الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-hādhā sababu kitmāni al-khabari ʿanka wa-ʿadami iʿlāmika bi-anna abāka al-maliku ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: So this is the cause of the concealing of the news from you, and the not-informing-you that your father is King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: That is why the story was kept from you, and why you were never told that your father is King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: ʿadam, “lack, absence”, before a verbal noun makes a negative: ʿadam iʿlāmika, “not informing you”. In bi-anna abāka al-maliku …, abāka is the subject of anna (accusative) and al-maliku its predicate (nominative), so ʿUmaru ibnu, in apposition, is nominative too.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَقَلَّيْتَ بِالْمَمْلَكَةِ أَخْبَرْتُكَ وَمَا أَمْكَنَنِي أَنْ أُعْلِمَكَ إِلَّا فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaqallayta bi-al-mamlakati akhbartuka wa-mā amkananī an uʿlimaka illā fī hādhā al-waqti yā malika al-zamāni
sentences.l: And when you became-independent in the kingdom I told you; and it was not possible-for-me to inform you except at this time, O king of the age.
sentences.i: Now that you rule the kingdom in your own right, I have told you; I could not let you know before this moment, O king of the age.
sentences.n: istaqallayta, “you took sole charge”, is printed with a shadda (استقلّيت): a Middle Arabic form of Classical istaqlalta, made on the pattern of doubled verbs such as ḥallayt for ḥalalt. istaqalla bi-, “to hold something independently, rule alone”. yā malika al-zamān, “O king of the age”, a courtly address; it rhymes with burhān in the next sentence.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ كَشَفْتُ لَكَ السِّرَّ وَالْبُرْهَانَ وَهَذَا مَاعِنْدِي مِنَ الْخَبَرِ وَأَنْتَ بِرَأْيِكَ أَخْبَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad kashaftu laka al-sirra wa-al-burhāna wa-hādhā mā ʿindī mina al-khabari wa-anta bi-raʾyika akhbaru
sentences.l: And I have uncovered for you the secret and the proof; and this is what is with me of the news, and you are with your judgement better-informed.
sentences.i: I have laid bare to you the secret and the proof of it. That is all I know of the matter, and you, by your own judgement, know best what to make of it.
sentences.n: The print runs mā and ʿindī together (ماعندي). akhbar, “better informed”, is an elative from the same root as khabar, “news”, giving the closing rhyme khabar / akhbar.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْأُسَارَى قَدْ سَمِعُوا مِنَ الْجَارِيَةِ مَرْجَانَةَ دَايَةِ الْمَلِكِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ جَمِيعَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-usārā qad samiʿū mina al-jāriyati Marjānata dāyati al-maliki hādhā al-kalāma jamīʿahu
sentences.l: And the captives had heard from the slave-woman Marjāna, the king's nurse, this speech, all of it.
sentences.i: Now the captives had heard every word of what Marjāna, the king's nurse, had said.
sentences.n: al-usārā, “the captives”, are Nuzhat al-Zamān and her company, at this point prisoners of Rūmzān. kāna … samiʿū: the verb kāna stays singular before a plural subject, as Classical allows.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا وَسَاعَتِهَا صَيْحَةً وَقَالَتْ هَذَا الْمَلِكُ رُومْزَانُ أَخِي مِنْ أَبِي عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥat Nuzhatu al-Zamāni min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā ṣayḥatan wa-qālat hādhā al-maliku Rūmzānu akhī min abī ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And Nuzhat al-Zamān cried-out, from her moment and her hour, a cry, and said: This King Rūmzān is my brother from my father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān,
sentences.i: At once Nuzhat al-Zamān gave a cry and said, “This King Rūmzān is my brother by my father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān,
sentences.n: min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā, “from her moment and her hour”, “there and then”. akhī min abī, “my brother on my father's side”, a half-brother. The sentence goes on in the next line with his mother's name.

sentences.t: وَأُمُّهُ الْمَلِكَةُ أَبْرِيزَةُ بِنْتُ الْمَلِكِ حَرْدُوبَ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ وَأَنَا أَعْرِفُ هَذِهِ الْجَارِيَةَ مَرْجَانَةَ حَقَّ الْمَعْرِفَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ummuhu al-malikatu Abrīzatu bintu al-maliki Ḥardūba maliki al-Rūmi wa-anā aʿrifu hādhihi al-jāriyata Marjānata ḥaqqa al-maʿrifati
sentences.l: and his mother is the queen Abrīza, daughter of the king Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm; and I know this slave-girl Marjāna the truth of knowing.
sentences.i: and his mother was Queen Abrīza, daughter of King Ḥardūb, king of the Rūm. And this slave-woman Marjāna I know full well!”
sentences.n: Nuzhat al-Zamān is still speaking; the sentence carries on from her cry that King Rūmzān is her brother by her father. ḥaqqa al-maʿrifati, “the truth of knowing”, an accusative of manner: “with true knowledge, thoroughly”. Marjāna had been Abrīza's servant, and so is known to Nuzhat al-Zamān from the old days.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ رُومْزَانُ هَذَا أَخَذَتْهُ الْحِدَّةُ وَصَارَ مُتَحَيِّرًا فِي أَمْرِهِ وَأَحْضَرَ فِي وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku Rūmzānu hādhā akhadhathu al-ḥiddatu wa-ṣāra mutaḥayyiran fī amrihi wa-aḥḍara fī waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi Nuzhata al-Zamāni bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: And when the king Rūmzān heard this, the agitation seized him, and he became bewildered in his affair; and he brought, in his time and his hour, Nuzhat al-Zamān between his hands.
sentences.i: When King Rūmzān heard this he was seized with agitation and at a loss what to make of it, and there and then he had Nuzhat al-Zamān brought before him.
sentences.n: ḥidda, “sharpness, vehemence”: a sudden heat of feeling.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهَا حَنَّ الدَّمُ لِلدَّمِ وَاسْتَخْبَرَهَا عَنْ قِصَّتِهِ فَحَكَتْ لَهُ الْقِصَّةَ فَوَافَقَ كَلَامُهَا كَلَامَ دَايَتِهِ مَرْجَانَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā ḥanna al-damu li-al-dami wa-istakhbarahā ʿan qiṣṣatihi fa-ḥakat lahu al-qiṣṣata fa-wāfaqa kalāmuhā kalāma dāyatihi Marjānata
sentences.l: And when he saw her, the blood yearned to the blood, and he asked-her-for-news about his story; and she told him the story, and her words agreed with the words of his nurse Marjāna.
sentences.i: When he saw her, blood called out to blood. He asked her to tell him his story, and she told it to him, and her account agreed with that of his nurse Marjāna.
sentences.n: ḥanna al-damu li-al-dami, “blood yearned for blood”: kinship makes itself felt before it is proved. The print marks the doubled nūn of ḥanna. qiṣṣatihi, “his story”, with the masculine pronoun: either the story of his own birth, or a slip for qiṣṣatihā, “her story”; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَصَحَّ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ أَنَّهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَكٍّ وَلَا ارْتِيَابٍ وَأَنَّ أَبَاهُ الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣaḥḥa ʿinda al-maliki annahu min ahli al-ʿIrāqi min ghayri shakkin wa-lā irtiyābin wa-anna abāhu al-maliku ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And it became-sound with the king that he was of the people of Iraq, without doubt and without misgiving, and that his father was the king ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: So the king was assured, beyond all doubt or question, that he was of the people of Iraq and that his father was King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: ṣaḥḥa ʿinda, “it was established in the mind of”. shakk / irtiyāb, a doubled pair for emphasis, both meaning doubt. The second anna governs abāhu (accusative) as its subject; al-maliku ʿUmaru is the predicate, in the nominative. The phrase ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān runs across a line end in the print.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ مِنْ تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ وَحَلَّ كِتَافَ أُخْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ فَقَدِمَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَتْ يَدَيْهِ وَدَمَعَتْ عَيْنَاهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāma min tilka al-sāʿati wa-ḥalla kitāfa ukhtihi Nuzhati al-Zamāni fa-qadimat ilayhi wa-qabbalat yadayhi wa-damaʿat ʿaynāhā
sentences.l: And he rose from that hour and untied the bonds of his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān; and she came to him and kissed his hands, and her two eyes shed-tears.
sentences.i: He rose that very moment and loosed the bonds of his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān. She came up to him and kissed his hands, her eyes brimming with tears.
sentences.n: qadima ilā, “to come to”. min tilka al-sāʿa, “from that hour”, i.e. at once. kitāf, the cord that ties a captive's arms behind the shoulders (katif); the print marks the doubled lām of ḥalla.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى الْمَلِكُ لِبُكَائِهَا وَأَخَذَتْهُ حَنِيَّةُ الْأُخُوَّةِ وَمَالَ قَلْبُهُ إِلَى ابْنِ أُخْتِهِ السُّلْطَانِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-bakā al-maliku li-bukāʾihā wa-akhadhathu ḥaniyyatu al-ukhuwwati wa-māla qalbuhu ilā ibni ukhtihi al-sulṭāni Kāna Mā Kāna
sentences.l: And the king wept for her weeping, and the tenderness of brotherhood took him, and his heart inclined toward the son of his sister, the sultan Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.i: The king wept to see her weep; a brother's tenderness came over him, and his heart went out to his nephew, Sultan Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.n: ḥaniyya, “tenderness, affection”, a later word beside Classical ḥanān. The print marks the doubled wāw of ukhuwwa, “brotherhood”. ibn ukhtihi, “his sister's son”: strictly Kān Mā Kān is the son of Rūmzān's brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and a few lines on Marjāna calls him “your brother's son”; the text is loose here, and the reading is kept.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ نَاهِضًا عَلَي قَدَمَيْهِ وَأَخَذَ السَّيْفَ مِنْ يَدِ السَّيَّافِ فَأَيْقَنَ الْأُسَارَى بِالْهَلَاكِ لَمَّا رَأَوْا مِنْهُ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma nāhiḍan ʿalā qadamayhi wa-akhadha al-sayfa min yadi al-sayyāfi fa-ayqana al-usārā bi-al-halāki lammā raʾaw minhu dhālika
sentences.l: And he stood rising on his two feet and took the sword from the hand of the swordsman; and the captives were-certain of the perishing when they saw that from him.
sentences.i: He sprang to his feet and took the sword from the executioner's hand, and the captives, seeing this, were sure their end had come.
sentences.n: ʿalā is printed with a dotted yāʾ (علي); kept and pointed ʿalā. sayyāf, “swordsman”, the executioner who stands ready at the king's side.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِهِمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَفَكَّ وَثَاقَهُمْ وَقَالَ لِدَايَتِهِ مَرْجَانَةَ اشْرَحِي حَدِيثَكِ الَّذِي شَرَحْتِهِ لِي لِهَؤُلَاءِ الْجَمَاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-amara bi-iḥḍārihim bayna yadayhi wa-fakka wathāqahum wa-qāla li-dāyatihi Marjānata ishraḥī ḥadīthaki alladhī sharaḥtihi lī li-hāʾulāʾi al-jamāʿati
sentences.l: And he ordered the bringing of them between his hands, and loosed their bond, and said to his nurse Marjāna: Set-out your account which you set-out to me, to these the company.
sentences.i: But he ordered them brought before him and had their bonds undone, and said to his nurse Marjāna, “Tell these people the story you told me.”
sentences.n: sharaḥa, “to lay open, explain in full”. sharaḥtihi, “you set it out”: the feminine ending -ti with the long vowel before the pronoun, sharaḥtīhi, is the Classical form; the shorter form is pointed here as the rasm suggests. jamāʿa, “company, group”, treated as a plural: hāʾulāʾi al-jamāʿa, “these people”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ دَايَتُهُ مَرْجَانَةُ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ هَذَا الشَّيْخَ هُوَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَهُوَ لِي أَكْبَرُ شَاهِدٍ لِأَنَّهُ يَعْرِفُ حَقِيقَةَ الْأَمْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat dāyatuhu Marjānatu iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna hādhā al-shaykha huwa al-wazīru Dandānu wa-huwa lī akbaru shāhidin li-annahu yaʿrifu ḥaqīqata al-amri
sentences.l: And his nurse Marjāna said: Know, O king, that this old-man is the vizier Dandān, and he is for me the greatest witness, because he knows the truth of the matter.
sentences.i: His nurse Marjāna said, “Know, O king, that this old man is the vizier Dandān, and he is my best witness, for he knows how matters truly stand.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا وَسَاعَتِهَا وَعَلَى مَنْ حَضَرَهُمْ مِنْ مُلُوكِ الرُّومِ وَمُلُوكِ الْإِفْرَنْجِ وَحَدَّثَتْهُمْ بِذَلِكَ الْحَدِيثِ وَالْمَلِكَةُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُمَا مِنَ الْأُسَارَى يُصَدِّقُونَهَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā aqbalat ʿalayhim min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā wa-ʿalā man ḥaḍarahum min mulūki al-Rūmi wa-mulūki al-Ifranji wa-ḥaddathathum bi-dhālika al-ḥadīthi wa-al-malikatu Nuzhatu al-Zamāni wa-al-wazīru Dandānu wa-man maʿahumā mina al-usārā yuṣaddiqūnahā ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: Then she turned to them, from her time and her hour, and to whoever was present with them of the kings of the Rūm and the kings of the Franks, and she told them that account, while the queen Nuzhat al-Zamān and the vizier Dandān and whoever was with them-two of the captives were confirming her in that.
sentences.i: Then and there she turned to them, and to all the kings of the Rūm and of the Franks who were present, and told them the whole story, while Queen Nuzhat al-Zamān, the vizier Dandān and the captives with them bore her out in every point.
sentences.n: aqbala ʿalā, “to turn to, face”. al-Ifranj, “the Franks”, the Western Europeans. The last clause, wa-al-malikatu …, is a circumstantial (ḥāl) clause opened by wāw: “while the queen … were confirming”. ṣaddaqa ʿalā, “to bear someone out in”.

sentences.t: وَفِي آخِرِ الْحَدِيثِ لَاحَتْ مِنَ الْجَارِيَةِ مَرْجَانَةَ الْتِفَاتَةٌ فَرَأَتِ الْخَرَزَةَ الثَّالِثَةَ بِعَيْنِهَا رَفِيقَةَ الْخَرَزَتَيْنِ اللَّتَيْنِ كَانَتَا مَعَ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ فِي رَقَبَةِ السُّلْطَانِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ فَعَرَفَتْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-fī ākhiri al-ḥadīthi lāḥat mina al-jāriyati Marjānata iltifātatun fa-raʾati al-kharazata al-thālithata bi-ʿaynihā rafīqata al-kharazatayni allatayni kānatā maʿa al-malikati Abrīzata fī raqabati al-sulṭāni Kāna Mā Kāna fa-ʿarafathā
sentences.l: And at the end of the account there gleamed from the slave-woman Marjāna a glance, and she saw the third bead itself, the companion of the two beads which had been with the queen Abrīza, on the neck of the sultan Kān Mā Kān, and she knew it.
sentences.i: As the story drew to its end, Marjāna happened to glance aside, and there on the neck of Sultan Kān Mā Kān she saw the third bead, the very fellow of the two that Queen Abrīza had had, and she knew it at once.
sentences.n: The print has التقانة, a misprint for التفاتة, “a glance”, corrected here. lāḥat minhu iltifātatun, “a glance gleamed from him”, is the stock phrase for a chance look aside. The three beads (kharaza) are the jewels that King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān once gave his children; Abrīza had one of them, and they serve as tokens of recognition. bi-ʿaynihā, “itself, the very one”.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَتْ صَيْحَةً عَظِيمَةً دَوَى لَهَا الْفَضَاءُ وَقَالَتْ لِلْمَلِكِ يَا وَلَدِي اعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ قَدْ زَادَ فِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ صِدْقُ يَقِينِي
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥat ṣayḥatan ʿaẓīmatan dawā lahā al-faḍāʾu wa-qālat li-al-maliki yā waladī iʿlam annahu qad zāda fī tilka al-sāʿati ṣidqu yaqīnī
sentences.l: And she cried a great cry for which the open-space resounded, and she said to the king: O my child, know that in that hour the truth of my certainty has increased,
sentences.i: She gave a great cry that rang through the open air, and said to the king, “My son, know that at this moment my certainty has been made surer still,
sentences.n: dawā, “to resound, echo”; faḍāʾ, “open space, the air”. ṣidq yaqīnī, “the truth of my certainty”. The sentence goes on in the next unit with li-anna, “because”.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّ هَذِهِ الْخَرَزَةَ الَّتِي فِي رَقَبَةِ هَذَا الْأَسِيرِ نَظِيرُ الْخَرَزَةِ الَّتِي وَضَعْتُهَا فِي عُنُقِكَ وَهِيَ رَفِيقَتُهَا وَهَذَا الْأَسِيرُ هُوَ ابْنُ أَخِيكَ وَهُوَ كَانَ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: li-anna hādhihi al-kharazata allatī fī raqabati hādhā al-asīri naẓīru al-kharazati allatī waḍaʿtuhā fī ʿunuqika wa-hiya rafīqatuhā wa-hādhā al-asīru huwa ibnu akhīka wa-huwa Kāna Mā Kāna
sentences.l: because this bead which is on the neck of this captive is the counterpart of the bead which I put on your neck, and it is its companion; and this captive is the son of your brother, and he is Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.i: for the bead on this captive's neck is the match of the one I hung about your own neck, its very fellow. This captive is your brother's son: he is Kān Mā Kān.”
sentences.n: naẓīr, “equal, counterpart”. raqaba and ʿunuq both mean “neck”, used here side by side for variety. ibn akhīka, “your brother's son”: Kān Mā Kān is the son of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, Rūmzān's half-brother.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ مَرْجَانَةَ الْتَفَتَتْ إِلَى كَانَ مَا كَانَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَرِنِي هَذِهِ الْخَرَزَةَ يَا مَلِكَ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-jāriyata Marjānata iltafatat ilā Kāna Mā Kāna wa-qālat lahu arinī hādhihi al-kharazata yā malika al-zamāni
sentences.l: Then the slave-woman Marjāna turned to Kān Mā Kān and said to him: Show me this bead, O king of the age.
sentences.i: Then Marjāna turned to Kān Mā Kān and said, “Show me that bead, O king of the age.”
sentences.n: arinī, “show me”, the imperative of Form IV arā (from raʾā, “to see”) with the suffix -nī. malik al-zamān, “king of the age”, a courtly form of address.

sentences.t: فَنَزَعَهَا مِنْ عُنُقِهِ وَنَاوَلَهَا لِتِلْكَ الْجَارِيَةِ دَايَةِ الْمَلِكِ رُومْزَانَ فَأَخَذَتْهَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-nazaʿahā min ʿunuqihi wa-nāwalahā li-tilka al-jāriyati dāyati al-maliki Rūmzāna fa-akhadhathā minhu
sentences.l: And he pulled it off from his neck and handed it to that slave-woman, the nurse of the king Rūmzān, and she took it from him.
sentences.i: He drew it off his neck and handed it to the woman, King Rūmzān's nurse, and she took it from him.
sentences.n: nāwala, “to hand over”, takes the person directly in Classical (nāwalahā iyyāhā); here the person receiving comes with li-, as in spoken usage.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَأَلَتْ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ عَنِ الْخَرَزَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ فَأَعْطَتْهَا لَهَا
sentences.tr: thumma saʾalat Nuzhata al-Zamāni ʿani al-kharazati al-thālithati fa-aʿṭathā lahā
sentences.l: Then she asked Nuzhat al-Zamān about the third bead, and she gave it to her.
sentences.i: Then she asked Nuzhat al-Zamān for the third bead, and Nuzhat al-Zamān gave it to her.
sentences.n: saʾala ʿan, “to ask about, ask for”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَارَ الْخَرَزَتَانِ فِي يَدِ الْجَارِيَةِ نَاوَلَتْهَا لِلْمَلِكِ رُومْزَانَ فَظَهَرَ لَهُ الْحَقُّ وَالْبُرْهَانُ وَتَحَقَّقَ أَنَّهُ عَمُّ السُّلْطَانِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ وَأَنَّ أَبَاهُ الْمَلِكُ عُمَرُ بْنُ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣāra al-kharazatāni fī yadi al-jāriyati nāwalathā li-al-maliki Rūmzāna fa-ẓahara lahu al-ḥaqqu wa-al-burhānu wa-taḥaqqaqa annahu ʿammu al-sulṭāni Kāna Mā Kāna wa-anna abāhu al-maliku ʿUmaru ibnu al-Nuʿmāni
sentences.l: And when the two-beads came-to-be in the hand of the slave-girl, she handed them to King Rūmzān; and there appeared to him the truth and the proof, and he made-certain that he was the paternal-uncle of the sultan Kān Mā Kān, and that his father was King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: When the slave-woman had the two beads in her hand, she passed them to King Rūmzān, and the truth stood plain before him, with its proof: he was certain now that he was the uncle of Sultan Kān Mā Kān, and that his own father was King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.n: ṣāra al-kharazatāni, “the two beads came to be”: a masculine verb before a feminine dual subject, a loose agreement common in this prose; ṣāra fī yadihā here simply means “got into her hand”. nāwalathā, “she handed them”, uses the feminine singular pronoun for the pair, as Middle Arabic often does for things. Rhyme: burhān, Nuʿmān. The beads are of one set from King ʿUmar's house, so the match proves Rūmzān to be ʿUmar's son and the half-brother of Kān Mā Kān's father. The slave-woman is Marjāna.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَعَانَقَهُ ثُمَّ عَانَقَ الْمَلِكَ كَانَ مَا كَانَ وَعَلَا الصِّيَاحُ بِكَثْرَةِ الْأَفْرَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi ilā al-wazīri Dandāna wa-ʿānaqahu thumma ʿānaqa al-malika Kāna Mā Kāna wa-ʿalā al-ṣiyāḥu bi-kathrati al-afrāḥi
sentences.l: So he rose, from his time and his hour, to the vizier Dandān and embraced him; then he embraced King Kān Mā Kān; and the shouting rose high with the abundance of the joys.
sentences.i: He rose that very moment, went to the vizier Dandān and embraced him, and then embraced King Kān Mā Kān; and the cries rose high, so great was the rejoicing.
sentences.n: bi-kathrat al-afrāḥ, “through the abundance of joys”: bi- gives the cause. Rhyme: ṣiyāḥ, afrāḥ.

sentences.t: وَفِي تِلْكَ السَّاعَةِ انْتَشَرَتِ الْبَشَائِرُ وَدُقَّتِ الْكَاسَاتُ وَالطُّبُولُ وَزُمِرَتِ الزُّمُورُ وَزَادَتِ الْأَفْرَاحُ
sentences.tr: wa-fī tilka al-sāʿati intasharati al-bashāʾiru wa-duqqati al-kāsātu wa-al-ṭubūlu wa-zumirati al-zumūru wa-zādati al-afrāḥu
sentences.l: And in that hour the glad-tidings spread, and the kettledrums and the drums were beaten, and the pipes were piped, and the joys increased.
sentences.i: In that hour the good news spread abroad; the kettledrums and drums were beaten, the pipes were played, and the rejoicing grew.
sentences.n: bashāʾir, plural of bishāra, “good news”, and also the celebration that greets it. kāsāt, plural of kāsa, here the kettledrums (or cymbals) of a military band, beside ṭubūl, “drums”. zumirati al-zumūru, “the pipes were piped”: zamara, “to play the reed pipe”, with its own noun as subject, a favourite jingle of the genre; read as passive, like duqqat.

sentences.t: وَسَمِعَ عَسَاكِرُ الْعِرَاقِ وَالشَّامِ ضَجِيجَ الرُّومِ بِالْأَفْرَاحِ فَرَكِبُوا عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ وَرَكِبَ الْمَلِكُ الزَّبَلْكَانُ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ يَا تُرَى مَا سَبَبُ هَذَا الصِّيَاحِ وَالسُّرُورِ الَّذِي فِي عَسْكَرِ الْإِفْرَنْجِ وَالرُّومِ
sentences.tr: wa-samiʿa ʿasākiru al-ʿIrāqi wa-al-Shāmi ḍajīja al-Rūmi bi-al-afrāḥi fa-rakibū ʿan ākhirihim wa-rakiba al-maliku al-Zabalkānu wa-qāla fī nafsihi yā turā mā sababu hādhā al-ṣiyāḥi wa-al-surūri alladhī fī ʿaskari al-Ifranji wa-al-Rūmi
sentences.l: And the armies of Iraq and Syria heard the clamour of the Rūm with the joys, and they mounted to the last of them; and King al-Zabalkān mounted, and said in himself: O, would one see, what is the cause of this shouting and the gladness that is in the army of the Franks and the Rūm?
sentences.i: The armies of Iraq and Syria heard the uproar of rejoicing among the Rūm, and they mounted, every last man of them. King al-Zabalkān mounted too, saying to himself, “What can be the cause of this shouting and merriment in the camp of the Franks and the Rūm?”
sentences.n: samiʿa ʿasākiru, “the armies heard”: a singular verb before a plural subject, as Classical allows. ʿan ākhirihim, “to the last of them”, meaning all without exception. yā turā, literally “O, is it seen?”, the colloquial “I wonder”, introducing a question to oneself. al-Ifranj, “the Franks”, the general word for western Christians; the text pairs them loosely with the Rūm, the Byzantines.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا عَسْكَرُ الْعِرَاقِ فَإِنَّهُمْ قَدْ أَقْبَلُوا وَعَلَى الْقِتَالِ عَوَّلُوا وَصَارُوا فِى الْمَيْدَانِ وَمَقَامِ الْحَرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā ʿaskaru al-ʿIrāqi fa-innahum qad aqbalū wa-ʿalā al-qitāli ʿawwalū wa-ṣārū fī al-maydāni wa-maqāmi al-ḥarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni
sentences.l: And as for the army of Iraq, they had advanced, and on fighting had resolved, and they came-to-be in the field and the standing-place of war and spear-thrusting.
sentences.i: As for the army of Iraq, they came on, set upon battle, and drew up on the field, in the place of war and the clash of spears.
sentences.n: ʿaskar, “army”, is singular, but the pronoun that takes it up is plural, fa-innahum, “they”: agreement by sense. ʿawwala ʿalā, “to resolve upon, rely on”; the object is put first, ʿalā al-qitāli ʿawwalū, to make the rhyme with aqbalū. Second rhyme: maydān, ṭiʿān. ṭiʿān, “thrusting with spears”, verbal noun of ṭāʿana.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ الْمَلِكُ رُومْزَانُ فَرَآى الْعَسَاكِرَ مُقْبِلِينَ وَلِلْحَرْبِ مُتَهَيِّئِينَ فَسَأَلَ عَنْ سَبَبِ ذَلِكَ فَأَخْبَرُوهُ بِالْخَبَرِ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata al-maliku Rūmzānu fa-raʾā al-ʿasākira muqbilīna wa-li-al-ḥarbi mutahayyiʾīna fa-saʾala ʿan sababi dhālika fa-akhbarūhu bi-al-khabari
sentences.l: And King Rūmzān turned and saw the armies advancing, and for war making-ready; and he asked about the cause of that, and they informed him of the news.
sentences.i: King Rūmzān turned and saw the armies advancing, ready for war. He asked what it meant, and they told him how matters stood.
sentences.n: فرآى, fa-raʾā, “and he saw”: the print spells raʾā with a madda alif and a final yāʾ, a variant spelling of رأى. muqbilīna, mutahayyiʾīna: two circumstantial accusatives, rhyming. The print marks the doubled yāʾ of mutahayyiʾīn, “making ready”. akhbarahu bi-al-khabar, “informed him of the news”, a cognate pair: “told him what had happened”.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ قَضَى فَكَانَ ابْنَةَ أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ أَنْ تَسِيرَ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا وَسَاعَتِهَا إِلَى عَسْكَرِ الشَّامِ وَالْعِرَاقِ وَتُعْلِمَهُمْ بِحُصُولِ الِاتِّفَاقِ وَأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ رُومْزَانَ ظَهَرَ أَنَّهُ عَمُّ السُّلْطَانِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-amara Qaḍā Fakāna ibnata akhīhi Sharrukāna an tasīra min waqtihā wa-sāʿatihā ilā ʿaskari al-Shāmi wa-al-ʿIrāqi wa-tuʿlimahum bi-ḥuṣūli al-ittifāqi wa-anna al-malika Rūmzāna ẓahara annahu ʿammu al-sulṭāni Kāna Mā Kāna
sentences.l: And he commanded Qaḍā Fakān, the daughter of his brother Sharrukān, that she go from her time and her hour to the army of Syria and Iraq and inform them of the coming-about of the agreement, and that King Rūmzān had come-to-light that he was the paternal-uncle of the sultan Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.i: He ordered Qaḍā Fakān, his brother Sharrukān's daughter, to go at once to the army of Syria and Iraq and tell them that peace had been made, and that King Rūmzān had turned out to be the uncle of Sultan Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.n: Sharrukān and Rūmzān are both sons of King ʿUmar, so Qaḍā Fakān is Rūmzān's niece. al-ittifāq, “the agreement”, here the reconciliation of the two camps; ittifāq can also mean a lucky coincidence, and both senses are in play. ẓahara annahu, “it came to light that he”: the king is made the subject of the verb whose real subject is the fact, “King Rūmzān appeared that he was”, a common loose construction.

sentences.t: فَسَارَتْ قَضَى فَكَانَ بِنَفْسِهَا وَنَفَتْ عَنْهَا الشُّرُورَ وَالْأَحْزَانَ حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ الزَّبَلْكَانِ وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَأَعْلَمَتْهُ بِمَا جَرَى مِنَ الِاتِّفَاقِ وَأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ رُومْزَانَ ظَهَرَ أَنَّهُ عَمُّهَا وَعَمُّ كَانَ مَا كَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-sārat Qaḍā Fakāna bi-nafsihā wa-nafat ʿanhā al-shurūra wa-al-aḥzāna ḥattā waṣalat ilā al-maliki al-Zabalkāni wa-sallamat ʿalayhi wa-aʿlamathu bi-mā jarā mina al-ittifāqi wa-anna al-malika Rūmzāna ẓahara annahu ʿammuhā wa-ʿammu Kāna Mā Kāna
sentences.l: So Qaḍā Fakān went in her own person, and cast-away from herself the evils and the sorrows, until she reached King al-Zabalkān, and greeted him, and informed him of what had happened of the agreement, and that King Rūmzān had come-to-light that he was her paternal-uncle and the paternal-uncle of Kān Mā Kān.
sentences.i: Qaḍā Fakān went herself, every care and sorrow cast aside, until she reached King al-Zabalkān. She greeted him and told him of the peace that had come about, and that King Rūmzān had turned out to be her uncle and Kān Mā Kān's.
sentences.n: bi-nafsihā, “in her own person”, herself rather than by a messenger. nafā ʿan, “to drive away from”; the print marks nafat with a fatḥa and a sukūn. Rhyme: aḥzān, al-Zabalkān.

sentences.t: وَحِينَ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَجَدَتْهُ بَاكِىَ الْعَيْنِ خَائِفًا عَلَى الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْأَعْيَانِ فَشَرَحَتْ لَهُ الْقِصَّةَ مِنْ أَوَّلِهَا إِلَى آخِرِهَا فَزَادَتْ أَفْرَاحُهُمْ وَزَالَتْ أَتْرَاحُهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥīna aqbalat ʿalayhi wajadathu bākiya al-ʿayni khāʾifan ʿalā al-umarāʾi wa-al-aʿyāni fa-sharaḥat lahu al-qiṣṣata min awwalihā ilā ākhirihā fa-zādat afrāḥuhum wa-zālat atrāḥuhum
sentences.l: And when she came-up to him she found him weeping of eye, fearing for the emirs and the notables; so she laid-out for him the story from its beginning to its end, and their joys increased and their griefs departed.
sentences.i: When she came to him she found him with tears in his eyes, fearing for the emirs and the nobles. She told him the whole story from beginning to end; their joy grew, and their sorrows vanished.
sentences.n: bākiya al-ʿayni, “weeping of eye”: an adjective governing a noun of specification, Classical and elegant; the print spells bākiya with a final ى, as it often writes yāʾ. aʿyān, “eyes”, hence “the notables, the eminent”. afrāḥ / atrāḥ, “joys / griefs”: the rhyming pair the sajʿ loves. tarḥ, “grief”, lives almost only in this pairing.

sentences.t: وَرَكِبَ الْمَلِكُ الزَّبَلْكَانُ هُوَ وَجَمِيعُ الْأَكَابِرِ وَالْأَعْيَانِ وَسَارَتْ قُدَّامَهُمُ الْمَلِكَةُ قَضَى فَكَانَ حَتَّى أَوْصَلَتْهُمْ إِلَى سُرَادِقِ الْمَلِكِ رُومْزَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-rakiba al-maliku al-Zabalkānu huwa wa-jamīʿu al-akābiri wa-al-aʿyāni wa-sārat quddāmahumu al-malikatu Qaḍā Fakāna ḥattā awṣalathum ilā surādiqi al-maliki Rūmzāna
sentences.l: And King al-Zabalkān mounted, he and all the great-ones and the notables, and Queen Qaḍā Fakān went before them until she brought them to the pavilion of King Rūmzān.
sentences.i: King al-Zabalkān mounted with all the grandees and nobles, and Queen Qaḍā Fakān rode before them until she had brought them to King Rūmzān's pavilion.
sentences.n: rakiba … huwa wa-jamīʿu, “he mounted, he and all”: the pronoun huwa is repeated so that others can be joined to the subject. surādiq, “a great tent, pavilion”, a Persian loanword. Qaḍā Fakān is called al-malika, “the queen”, as a princess of the royal house.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ وَجَدُوهُ جَالِسًا مَعَ ابْنِ أَخِيهِ السُّلْطَانِ كَانَ مَا كَانَ وَقَدِ اسْتَشَارَهُ هُوَ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ فِي أَمْرِ الْمَلِكِ الزَّبَلْكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā dakhalū ʿalayhi wajadūhu jālisan maʿa ibni akhīhi al-sulṭāni Kāna Mā Kāna wa-qadi istashārahu huwa wa-al-wazīru Dandānu fī amri al-maliki al-Zabalkāni
sentences.l: And when they came-in upon him, they found him sitting with the son of his brother, the sultan Kān Mā Kān, and he had consulted him, he and the vizier Dandān, in the matter of King al-Zabalkān.
sentences.i: When they came in to him, they found him sitting with his nephew, Sultan Kān Mā Kān, who with the vizier Dandān had been taking counsel with him about King al-Zabalkān.
sentences.n: istashārahu huwa wa-al-wazīru, “he consulted him, he and the vizier”: again huwa repeats the hidden subject so that the vizier can be added to it. Who consulted whom is not spelled out; the natural reading is that the young sultan and Dandān sought Rūmzān's advice, but the reverse is possible. Either way, the three of them decide together in what follows.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقُوا عَلَى أَنَّهُمْ يُسَلِّمُونَ إِلَيْهِ مَدِينَةَ دِمَشْقِ الشَّامِ وَيَتْرُكُونَهُ مَلِكًا عَلَيْهَا كَمَا كَانَ مِثْلَ الْعَادَةِ وَهُمْ يَدْخُلُونَ إِلَى الْعِرَاقِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqū ʿalā annahum yusallimūna ilayhi madīnata Dimashqi al-Shāmi wa-yatrukūnahu malikan ʿalayhā kamā kāna mithla al-ʿādati wa-hum yadkhulūna ilā al-ʿIrāqi
sentences.l: And they agreed on that they would hand-over to him the city of Damascus-of-Syria, and leave him king over it as he had been, like the custom, while they would enter into Iraq.
sentences.i: They agreed to hand over to him the city of Damascus and leave him king there as he had been before, while they themselves went on into Iraq.
sentences.n: Dimashq al-Shām, “Damascus of Syria”, the usual full name of the city; al-Shām is both Syria and, loosely, Damascus itself. kamā kāna mithla al-ʿāda, “as he was, like the custom”: a doubled phrase, “just as before”. wa-hum yadkhulūna, “while they enter”: a circumstantial clause with the imperfect, here of a plan for the future. Iraq, with Baghdad, is the seat of King ʿUmar's house.

sentences.t: فَجَعَلُوا الْمَلِكَ الزَّبَلْكَانَ عَامِلًا عَلَى دِمَشْقِ الشَّامِ
sentences.tr: fa-jaʿalū al-malika al-Zabalkāna ʿāmilan ʿalā Dimashqi al-Shāmi
sentences.l: So they made King al-Zabalkān governor over Damascus-of-Syria.
sentences.i: So they made King al-Zabalkān governor of Damascus.
sentences.n: ʿāmil, “one who works”, is the regular word for a provincial governor acting for the sovereign.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرُوهُ بِالتَّوَجُّهِ إِلَيْهَا فَتَوَجَّهَ بِعَسَاكِرِهِ إِلَيْهَا وَمَشَوْا مَعَهُ سَاعَةً لِأَجْلِ الْوَدَاعِ وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ رَجَعُوا إِلَى مَكَانِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma amarūhu bi-al-tawajjuhi ilayhā fa-tawajjaha bi-ʿasākirihi ilayhā wa-mashaw maʿahu sāʿatan li-ajli al-wadāʿi wa-baʿda dhālika rajaʿū ilā makānihim
sentences.l: Then they commanded him the setting-out to it, and he set-out with his armies to it; and they walked with him an hour for the sake of the farewell, and after that they returned to their place.
sentences.i: Then they bade him set out for it, and he set off there with his troops. They went along with him a while to see him off, and afterwards returned to their own camp.
sentences.n: amara bi-, “to order (something)”: the verb takes its object with bi-, so bi-al-tawajjuh, “ordered him to set out”. tawajjaha ilā, “to turn toward, make for”; bi-ʿasākirihi, “with his armies”, bi- of accompaniment. li-ajli, “for the sake of”. sāʿa, “an hour”, often just “a while”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَادَوْا فِى الْعَسْكَرِ بِالرَّحِيلِ إِلَى بِلَادِ الْعِرَاقِ وَاجْتَمَعَ الْعَسْكَرَانِ مَعَ بَعْضِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma nādaw fī al-ʿaskari bi-al-raḥīli ilā bilādi al-ʿIrāqi wa-ijtamaʿa al-ʿaskarāni maʿa baʿḍihim
sentences.l: Then they called-out in the army the departure to the lands of Iraq, and the two-armies joined together with one-another.
sentences.i: Then they had the march to Iraq proclaimed through the camp, and the two armies joined into one.
sentences.n: nādā bi-, “to proclaim”: what is announced takes bi-. maʿa baʿḍihim, “with each other”, the colloquial reciprocal, used here of the two armies with a plural pronoun.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمُلُوكَ قَالُوا لِبَعْضِهِمْ مَا بَقِيَتْ قُلُوبُنَا تَسْتَرِيحُ وَلَا يُشْفَى غَيْظُنَا إِلَّا بِأَخْذِ الثَّأْرِ وَكَشْفِ الْعَارِ بِالِانْتِقَامِ مِنَ الْعَجُوزِ شَوَاهِي الْمُلَقَّبَةِ بِذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-mulūka qālū li-baʿḍihim mā baqiyat qulūbunā tastarīḥu wa-lā yushfā ghayẓunā illā bi-akhdhi al-thaʾri wa-kashfi al-ʿāri bi-al-intiqāmi mina al-ʿajūzi Shawāhī al-mulaqqabati bi-Dhāti al-Dawāhī
sentences.l: Then the kings said to one-another: Our hearts will no longer rest, nor will our rage be healed, except by the taking of the blood-revenge and the removing of the shame, by vengeance on the old-woman Shawāhī, the surnamed Dhāt al-Dawāhī.
sentences.i: Then the kings said to one another, “Our hearts will know no rest and our rage no cure until we have taken our blood-revenge and wiped out our shame by vengeance on the old woman Shawāhī, called Dhāt al-Dawāhī.”
sentences.n: mā baqiyat … tastarīḥu, “no longer will … rest”: baqiya with a negative and an imperfect is colloquial for “no longer”. thaʾr, “blood-revenge”, rhymes with ʿār, “shame”; kashf al-ʿār, literally “uncovering, lifting the shame”. laqqaba bi-, “to give the nickname”. She had a hand in the death of King ʿUmar and of Sharrukān.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ سَارَ الْمَلِكُ رُومْزَانُ مَعَ خَوَاصِّهِ وَأَرْبَابِ دَوْلَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika sāra al-maliku Rūmzānu maʿa khawāṣṣihi wa-arbābi dawlatihi
sentences.l: And at that King Rūmzān set-out with his intimates and the lords of his state.
sentences.i: At that King Rūmzān set out with his intimates and the great men of his realm.
sentences.n: khawāṣṣ, “intimates, the inner circle”, plural of khāṣṣa. arbāb al-dawla, “the lords of the state”, the ministers and officers of the court.

sentences.t: وَفَرِحَ السُّلْطَانُ كَانَ مَا كَانَ بِعَمِّهِ الْمَلِكِ رُومْزَانَ وَدَعَا لِلْجَارِيَةِ مَرْجَانَةَ حَيْثُ عَرَّفَتْهُمْ بِبَعْضِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-fariḥa al-sulṭānu Kāna Mā Kāna bi-ʿammihi al-maliki Rūmzāna wa-daʿā li-al-jāriyati Marjānata ḥaythu ʿarrafathum bi-baʿḍihim
sentences.l: And the sultan Kān Mā Kān rejoiced in his paternal-uncle King Rūmzān, and prayed for the slave-girl Marjāna, since she had made-them-known to one-another.
sentences.i: Sultan Kān Mā Kān rejoiced in his uncle King Rūmzān, and called down blessings on the slave-woman Marjāna for having made them known to each other.
sentences.n: fariḥa bi-, “to rejoice in”. daʿā li-, “to pray for”, invoke good upon (daʿā ʿalā is to curse). ʿarrafa bi-, “to acquaint with, make known to”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَارُوا وَلَمْ يَزَالُو سَائِرِينَ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى أَرْضِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma sārū wa-lam yazālū sāʾirīna ḥattā waṣalū ilā arḍihim
sentences.l: Then they journeyed, and did not cease journeying until they arrived at their land.
sentences.i: Then they set off, and travelled on without a halt until they reached their own country.
sentences.n: yazālū: the print leaves off the silent alif that Classical spelling writes after the plural ending (يزالوا), a frequent habit of the edition. lam yazālū sāʾirīna, “they did not cease travelling”, the stock way of covering a long journey in one breath.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ بِهِمُ الْحَاجِبُ الْكَبِيرُ سَاسَانُ فَطَلَعَ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَ الْمَلِكِ رُومْزَانَ فَخَلَعَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa bihimu al-ḥājibu al-kabīru Sāsānu fa-ṭalaʿa wa-qabbala yada al-maliki Rūmzāna fa-khalaʿa ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And the Great Chamberlain Sāsān heard of them, and went-out and kissed the hand of King Rūmzān; and he bestowed-a-robe upon him.
sentences.i: The Great Chamberlain Sāsān heard of their coming. He went out and kissed King Rūmzān's hand, and the king bestowed a robe of honour on him.
sentences.n: samiʿa bi-, “to hear of”. Sāsān, who had seized the throne, is called here by his old title, al-ḥājib al-kabīr, “the Great Chamberlain”, and comes out to meet the kings humbly. ṭalaʿa, “to go up, go out”, colloquial for going forth. khalaʿa ʿalā, “to put a robe of honour on someone”, the regular mark of royal favour; the subject shifts to Rūmzān without being named.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ رُومْزَانَ جَلَسَ وَأَجْلَسَ ابْنَ أَخِيهِ السُّلْطَانَ كَانَ مَا كَانَ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika Rūmzāna jalasa wa-ajlasa ibna akhīhi al-sulṭāna Kāna Mā Kāna ilā jānibihi
sentences.l: Then King Rūmzān sat, and seated the son of his brother, the sultan Kān Mā Kān, at his side.
sentences.i: Then King Rūmzān took his seat, and seated his nephew, Sultan Kān Mā Kān, beside him.
sentences.n: jalasa wa-ajlasa, “sat and seated”: the causative form IV of the same root.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ كَانَ مَا كَانَ إِلَى عَمِّهِ الْمَلِكِ رُومْزَانَ يَا عَمِّ مَا يَصْلُحُ هَذَا الْمُلْكُ إِلَّا لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Kāna Mā Kāna ilā ʿammihi al-maliki Rūmzāna yā ʿammi mā yaṣluḥu hādhā al-mulku illā laka
sentences.l: And Kān Mā Kān said to his paternal-uncle King Rūmzān: O my uncle, this kingship is not fitting except for you.
sentences.i: Kān Mā Kān said to his uncle King Rūmzān, “Uncle, this kingdom is fit for no one but you.”
sentences.n: qāla ilā, “said to”: Middle Arabic, where Classical says qāla li-. yā ʿammi, “O my uncle”, with the “my” shortened to its kasra. mā yaṣluḥu … illā laka, “it is not fit except for you”: mā is the plain colloquial negative with the imperfect. al-mulk, “kingship, kingdom”, is written exactly like al-malik, “the king”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ أَنْ أُعَارِضَكَ فِي مُلْكِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu maʿādha Allāhi an uʿāriḍaka fī mulkika
sentences.l: And he said to him: Refuge of God, that I should contest-you in your kingship!
sentences.i: Rūmzān answered, “God forbid that I should dispute your kingdom with you!”
sentences.n: maʿādha Allāh, “(I seek) the refuge of God”, an accusative of exclamation: “God forbid”. an uʿāriḍaka, “that I oppose you”: what is warded off follows with an.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَشَارَ عَلَيْهِمَا الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الِاثْنَانِ فِى الْمُلْكِ سَوَاءً وَكُلُّوَاحِدٍ يَحْكُمُ يَوْمًا فَارْتَضَيَا بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ashāra ʿalayhimā al-wazīru Dandānu an yakūna al-ithnāni fī al-mulki sawāʾan wa-kullu wāḥidin yaḥkumu yawman fa-irtaḍayā bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And at that the vizier Dandān counselled them both that the two be equal in the kingship, and each-one rule a day; and they were both content with that.
sentences.i: At that the vizier Dandān advised the two of them to share the kingdom as equals, each ruling on alternate days; and both agreed to it.
sentences.n: ashāra ʿalā, “to advise, counsel (someone)”. The print runs kull wāḥid, “each one”, together as one word, كلواحد. wa-kullu wāḥidin yaḥkumu yawman, “and each one rules a day”: a nominal clause carrying on the plan. irtaḍā bi-, “to be content with, accept”, here in the dual.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she ceased the speech allowed her.
